title: Building AI for Lawyers - Jacob Lauritzen, CTO of Legora
author: Basil Chatha
description: Evals without traces, million-cell tabular reviews, and cracks in the billable hour as a business model
summary: In this episode, we chat with Jacob Lauritzen, CTO of Legora, following the announcement of their $550M Series E at an $8.8B valuation a couple weeks ago. We talk about what it takes to build AI agents for lawyers and what other people building agents can learn from that work.
takeaways: We asked Jacob how you evaluate agents when you can't see your customers' data, which tasks still need better models, how legal engineers and forward deployed engineers split the work, and why the billable hour as a business model is being upended.
Jump to the billing model discussion → Evals without access to customer data Most teams improve their agents by reading traces.
Legora started in a Stockholm basement with a simple product: ChatGPT, Swedish law, and a search tool.
